page: Microsoft Azure M96lds_v4 is an enterprise-tier memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1536 GB of system memory, delivering a memory density of 16 GB per virtual core. The platform includes 3543 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage for low-latency operational workloads, in addition to supporting Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned by default.

The instance architecture is designed for memory-intensive computations where throughput and data capacity exceed conventional ratios. Having 96 dedicated processor threads allows the system to sustain extensive parallel compute tasks, while the 1.5 TB memory allocation allows complete datasets to reside directly in RAM. The 3543 GB local NVMe SSD subsystem provides high-throughput ephemeral caching, indexing, and scratch space, preventing I/O bottlenecks during data shuffling or temporary storage operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M96lds_v4 consolidates extreme memory capacity and dedicated compute into a single node, which can reduce licensing and operational overhead relative to multi-node clusters. A primary architectural tradeoff is the non-persistent nature of the bundled NVMe disk, necessitating network-attached persistent storage for durable state. This server type is intended for large-scale enterprise databases, in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, extensive Redis or Memcached deployments, enterprise data warehousing, and distributed data analytics.
